linkedin.text:
For six weeks I photographed one street between 2 AM and 4 AM.

Same 400 metres of Kettle Lane every night. One camera, one 35mm lens, no flash, no tripod. If the street was too dark, the frame was too dark.

I expected silence. I got a schedule.

At about 3:10 the bakery on the corner switches on its ovens.

At 3:40 the bins go out, and for eleven minutes the street is louder than it is at lunchtime.

Near number 27, a fox crossed on 31 of the 42 nights I logged.

In the same six weeks, 9 people walked the full length of the street.

That became the argument of my thesis: an empty street is never empty. It is working for somebody else. The bakers, the bin crew, the fox.

The 48 frames that made the edit will hang at the graduate show in June.

What does your street do while you sleep?

#Photography #StreetPhotography #Thesis

instagram.caption:
I spent six weeks on one street between 2 AM and 4 AM, expecting silence.

Instead I found a timetable. Ovens at 3:10. Bins at 3:40. A fox near number 27 most nights. Nine people in six weeks.

This is my BFA thesis, Night Shift: 48 frames, one 35mm lens, no flash. If the street was too dark, the frame was too dark.

Graduate show in June. Full project: link in bio.
